# D284 — The overnight long

**Status:** PRE-REGISTERED. Committed **before the runner exists**. Nothing here is a result.
**Date:** 2026-09-02
**Area:** Strategy research · **personal track**

---

## THIS HYPOTHESIS IS POST-HOC, AND THAT IS THE FIRST THING THE RECORD SAYS

**It was generated by looking at results.** [D282](D282-the-overnight-only-short.md) scored an
overnight *short* of the ten lowest-`hist_L` names and measured **−24.10 bp/night**. This study is
the arithmetic mirror of that cell: if shorting them loses 24 bp a night, buying them earns it.

**That does not make it illegitimate. It makes the disclosure load-bearing.**

| what shaped this search space | size |
|---|---:|
| [D280](D280-the-forecast-precheck.md) statistics, five parts | **165 (161 distinct)**, median largest \|t\| under the null **2.86** |
| D256 cells | 21 |
| D279 cells | 20 |
| D281 cells | 10 |
| D282 cells (**run**, so they count) | 19 |
| D283 cells | 26 |
| **carried under [R13](../RULES.md#r13)** | **96** |
| fresh here | 10 |
| **total** | **106** |

**The true multiplicity is larger than 106**, because the *direction* was chosen after seeing the
sign audit. No floor computed from ten cells can price that, and the record says so rather than
implying the F hurdle handles it.

**And it does not serve the stated aim.** The principal's objective is *a short edge in a rising
market*. **This is a long.** It is run because it is the only construction in the programme with a
measured per-trade move that exceeds its own cost bar, and refusing to look at it because the sign
is inconvenient would be choosing the conclusion. That tension is recorded, not resolved.

---

## The measurement this rests on

[D282](D282-the-overnight-only-short.md), hurdle M, on **31,831 scored trades**, dividends charged:

| cell | move bp | raw gap | div drag | trades |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `base\|all` — short every live name overnight | −5.657 | −4.783 | +0.874 | 2,620,292 |
| **`hist_L\|top10`** — short the 10 lowest | **−24.100** | −21.883 | +2.217 | 31,831 |
| `hist_L\|rnd10` — matched-count random | −6.636 | −5.828 | +0.808 | 31,842 |
| `hist_L\|per10` — persistent random | −5.713 | −4.481 | +1.231 | 31,846 |

Read for a long: **the selected names ROSE 21.883 bp overnight and paid 2.217 bp of dividends**,
so a long earned ~**+24.10 bp** against a **10 bp** round trip — `2c` cleared by **2.41×**.

**It is not the overnight risk premium.** Shorting *everything* moves −5.657 bp, so the universe's
own overnight drift is ~+5.7 bp for a long and **the selection adds ~18.4 bp on top of it.**

**And a long has no borrow.** Borrow was the constraint that made every short cell's breakeven
negative. It does not exist on this side.

**Turnover confounds cannot arise.** D282 measured `rnd-N` and `per-N` turnover ratios at **1.00×** —
a nightly book trades every night regardless of selection. The control defect that wrecked hurdle C
in D279 and D281 is structurally absent here.

---

## The construction

```
universe   ALL live, warm names on us_shorts_daily_raw.csv.gz -- 1,573 names,
           35.7% dead, ragged. The population D282 measured on.

score      hist_L from signals_ragged, LAGGED ONE BAR (R9)

arm        LONG the N LOWEST lagged hist_L.  N in {10, 25, 50}
window     enter at close(t), exit at open(t+1). OVERNIGHT ONLY.

controls   rnd-N   N drawn at random each night, matched count
           per-N   persistent random, matched turnover
           base    LONG every live name overnight  <-- the risk-premium control
```

**Cells: 3 N × 3 modes + 1 base = 10.** The QUAL universe is **not** tested; D282's measurement was
on ALL and adding a second universe would double the cells for no declared question.

**Costs.** 5 bp/side, `rf` 4% charged as financing on the long leg, PPY 252, **no borrow — longs do
not borrow, and this is a real asymmetry against every prior study rather than a favour granted
here.** Dividends are **received**, not paid; the runner must flip the sign D282 used and prove it
did (see the self-check below).

---

## THE CONFOUND MOST LIKELY TO KILL THIS, and it is not the risk premium

**BID-ASK BOUNCE.** The lowest-`hist_L` names are the ones that just fell hardest. Buying at the
**close** and selling at the **open** of names that just fell is the textbook setup for capturing a
*spread artifact* rather than a return: if the closing trade prints at the bid and the opening
trade prints nearer the mid, the measured close-to-open "gap" contains bounce that no one can
trade.

**This is the single most likely explanation for a +24 bp overnight effect concentrated in
just-fallen names, and it is declared before the run rather than discovered after.**

Two things make it worse on this fixture, both measured facts rather than worries:

- **[D264](D264-the-intraday-short-on-single-names.md) established that cost in basis points is
  inversely proportional to PRICE**, not to notional — commission ranged **0.20 bp (RH) to 4.15 bp
  (CLF)** inside one stratum. A flat 5 bp/side is therefore *optimistic for cheap names*.
- **A dead-inclusive universe skews the lowest-`hist_L` tail toward distressed, low-priced names**,
  which is exactly where the true spread is widest.

**Therefore the PRIMARY cost statistic is the BREAKEVEN HALF-SPREAD in bp/side** — the fee at which
net return reaches zero — reported the way `breakeven_bps` was in D264. It is a property of the
book rather than of my 5 bp assumption. **Reported beside it: the median PRICE of held names, and
the 10th percentile**, so the reader can judge whether 5 bp/side is remotely plausible for them.

**If the breakeven half-spread is below ~15 bp/side, this study is closed regardless of its
Sharpe**, because a book of low-priced just-fallen names will not trade at a tighter spread than
that in size.

---

## Hurdles

| | standard |
|---|---|
| **M** | **Mean move per trade ≥ 2c = 10 bp/night.** [D265](D265-the-entry-time-reconciliation.md)'s form, in which the trade count cancels and the hit rate never appears. **PRIMARY.** |
| **B** | **Breakeven half-spread ≥ 15 bp/side.** The confound above, made a hurdle rather than a caveat |
| **V** | **Positive net CAGR** after fees and financing |
| **C** | **Beats ALL THREE controls** — `rnd-N`, `per-N` **and `base`** — on Sharpe *and* money, **gross and net**. Beating `base` is what separates selection from the overnight risk premium |
| **F** | **Best-of-10 floor** (D228), one shared offset vector |
| **E′** | **Effective independent instruments ≥ 3.0 over the HELD BOOK**, and ≥500 trades |
| **H** | Rotation null — **REPORTED, NOT DECISIVE** |

**H is reported and cannot carry a verdict**, under [R7](../RULES.md#r7)'s corollary and three
measured demonstrations: D279's `S1_short|all` cleared it at the 100th percentile on both legs at
−0.757 Sharpe; D281 saw a *random* control clear it at the 100th while losing money; D283's
`ALL|per25` did the same.

**E′ is expected to degenerate and its number must not be over-read.** D279 scored **28.00 on 28
names**, D281 **63.00 on 63**, D283's `QUAL|per50` **87.91 on 88** — an identity correlation matrix,
because almost no *pair* of names in a rotating book shares the 250-bar overlap minimum. **If E′
comes back ≈ N, the runner must say so in the output**, and the hurdle is treated as passed-but-
uninformative rather than passed.

---

## Predictions

| | prediction | direction | confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **L1** | **M clears at all three N.** *This is near-determined by D282's mirror and must NOT be scored as a success* — it is stated so that a failure would be informative, not so a pass can be claimed | neutral | **very high** |
| **L2** | **The book beats `base` (long everything overnight) on GROSS Sharpe at all three N.** This is the real test: selection, or risk premium | **for** | **moderate** |
| **L3** | **The breakeven half-spread comes in BELOW 15 bp/side and hurdle B fails**, i.e. the effect is bid-ask bounce in cheap just-fallen names rather than a tradeable return | **AGAINST** | **moderate-high** |
| **L4** | **Net Sharpe is below 1.0 at every N even where M clears**, because a per-trade move that clears its cost bar does not imply a good risk-adjusted return — [D271](D271-the-trade-level-anatomy.md) found three arms whose *entire* profit sat in under 1% of trades, and removing the best 1% turned all three negative | **AGAINST** | **moderate** |

**L3 is the load-bearing prediction** and it is declared against the construction. **What would
falsify it: a breakeven half-spread of 15 bp/side or better at N = 25 on the ALL universe.** That
outcome would say the effect survives a spread three times the charged fee, and that bounce is not
the explanation.

**L4's falsifier: any cell with net Sharpe ≥ 1.0.**

## Look-ahead and sign self-checks — MANDATORY, both

[D279](D279-the-concentrated-short-on-dead-inclusive-names.md)'s first result was destroyed by
ranking with `score[:, t]` while earning bar `t`'s return, and D280 parts 3–5 were inverted by a
sign convention asserted in prose and never checked against money. **Both classes of error must be
excluded by assertion, not by care.**

1. **Lag audit** — re-derive the held set from `score[:, t−1]` in a second implementation that does
   **not** call `top_n`, and assert it matches at every bar and every N. The pattern is `audit_lag`
   in `scripts/run_unfiltered_ranking.py`.
2. **Sign audit** — assert on synthetic bars that a name which **rises** overnight produces a
   **positive** contribution for this LONG book, and that a dividend **increases** it rather than
   decreasing it. D282's runner asserts the opposite for a short; this one must assert the mirror
   and fail loudly if the sign was copied unchanged.
3. **Not-close-to-close** — assert the compounded grid differs materially from
   `panel.total_log_returns`, the defect that would be invisible in the output.

---

## Stop

**If M or B or C fails, the overnight long is closed** — no fourth N, no price filter added after
the fact, no alternative score, no second universe. **A price filter is the obvious post-hoc rescue
and it is pre-emptively refused here**; if cheap names carry the effect, that is the finding.

**If it clears, it is not a book entry.** Under [R8](../RULES.md#r8) it needs a pre-registered
out-of-sample test on a fixture this programme has not touched. **D246's reserved wide-universe
cohort is the candidate and is unspent.** `cohort3` is 15-minute intraday and is the wrong
instrument for a daily overnight book.

# AMENDMENT — appended 2026-09-02, BEFORE the runner was executed

**Everything above is preserved byte-for-byte. Nothing here is a result.** This adds **one
control** and tightens **one hurdle**. It adds no arm, varies no constant, and changes no
prediction that was declared for the construction.

## Why: D283 showed the existing controls cannot answer the question

[D283](D283-the-descending-ranking.md) ran after this record was committed and decomposed the
overnight move into a **direction-blind** part and a **directional** part, on the ALL universe, in
short bp:

```
        asc      dsc        c = (asc+dsc)/2      d = (asc-dsc)/2
N=10  -19.42   -9.93           -14.68                +4.75
N=25  -14.46   -5.14            -9.80                +4.66
N=50  -10.17   -2.98            -6.58                +3.60
```

**`c` is a TAIL TAX, not a signal.** `hist_L` is *signed acceleration*, so **both** of its tails
are the volatile names, and volatile names rise overnight whichever way they moved. **`d` — the
genuinely directional component — is real, correctly signed and stable at +3.6 to +4.8 bp**, and
it is 3–4× smaller than the tail effect sitting on top of it.

**So the ~+22 bp/night this study was built on decomposes as roughly +14.7 bp of tail premium and
+4.75 bp of `hist_L` direction.**

**And none of the three pre-registered controls sits in the tail.** `rnd-N` and `per-N` draw from
the whole universe; `base` is the whole universe. **All three would be beaten by the tail premium
alone, and hurdle C would return a pass meaning "volatile names rise overnight" — which D283 has
already established and which is not what this study asks.**

## The control that is added

```
tail-N   at each bar, take the 2N names with the most EXTREME |lagged hist_L|
         -- the N lowest and the N highest together -- and draw N of them AT
         RANDOM. Same N, same bars, same |score| magnitude, same volatility
         tail. The ONLY remaining difference from the treatment is WHICH TAIL.
```

**This isolates `d` from `c` by construction.** A book that beats `rnd-N`, `per-N` and `base` but
**not** `tail-N` has found the tail premium. A book that beats `tail-N` has found something in the
sign of `hist_L`.

**Cells: 3 N × 4 modes + 1 base = 13**, up from 10. **Ledger 96 carried + 13 fresh = 109.**
The best-of-K floor is computed over 13 rather than 10, and the disclosure above about the true
multiplicity being larger than any such floor is unchanged and still governs.

## Hurdle C is tightened

| | was | now |
|---|---|---|
| **C** | beats `rnd-N`, `per-N` and `base` | **beats `rnd-N`, `per-N`, `base` AND `tail-N`**, on Sharpe *and* money, gross and net |

**`tail-N` is the binding leg and is expected to be the one that fails.**

## Predictions — one restated, one added

**L2 is restated**, because as written it was answerable by the tail premium and therefore did not
test what it claimed:

| | prediction | direction | confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **L2′** | **The book beats `base` on gross Sharpe at all three N** — unchanged in substance, but it is now explicitly labelled as **the weak leg**, near-determined by the tail premium D283 measured, and **must not be read as evidence of selection** | neutral | **high** |
| **L5** | **The book does NOT beat `tail-N` on gross Sharpe at N = 25.** D283 puts the directional component at +4.66 bp against a tail premium of −9.80, so once the control shares the tail the residual is ~4.7 bp — under half the 10 bp round trip | **AGAINST** | **moderate-high** |

**L5 replaces L3 as the load-bearing prediction**, and both remain declared against the
construction. **What would falsify L5: the book beating `tail-N` on gross Sharpe at N = 25.** That
outcome would say the *sign* of `hist_L` carries overnight information beyond the volatility tail —
the first such finding in the programme.

**L1, L3 and L4 stand unamended.**

## What is NOT changed, so the amendment cannot be read as tuning

No arm is added, no N is added, no score is substituted, no universe is added, no constant is
varied, and no filter is introduced. **The stop clause stands, including its pre-emptive refusal of
a price filter added after the fact.** A control that makes an existing hurdle answer its own
question is not a degree of freedom spent on the result — it is one taken away.
